claim: In the MSSM with a bino-like chi0_1 LSP, stau-neutralino coannihilation sets the thermal relic density only when m_stau - m_chi is small; the prompt corridor m_tau < Delta m < ~60 GeV has no LHC sensitivity to DIRECT stau pair production, and a Phase-2 ISR/VBF + soft tau_h analysis/projection could cover it.
framework: R-parity-conserving MSSM (pMSSM/electroweak MSSM or SUGRA) with bino-like LSP and light stau NLSP (stau_R or mixed stau_1); simplified model pp -> stau stau (+ISR jet), stau -> tau chi0_1 (100%). Bundled but secondary: natural SUSY light stau_R with higgsino LSP; g-2 motivated light sleptons; Z'(B-L) -> slepton pairs (not in proposed target).
assumptions: Neutralino LSP is (mostly) bino, so that coannihilation (not mixing) controls Omega h^2
BR(stau -> tau chi0_1)=100%; electroweakinos and other sleptons decoupled (simplified model)
Stau chirality: pure stau_R (smallest cross section, typical NLSP) vs degenerate stau_L+stau_R (used by ATLAS 2609.37215)
controlling_parameters: stau L-R mixing angle (sets cross section, tau polarisation, sneutrino partner)
neutralino composition (bino fraction; higgsino/wino admixture opens larger Delta m and raises sigma_SI)
tan beta / mu (stau mixing; for g-2)
robust_predictions: Pure-bino stau coannihilation requires small Delta m: <~10 GeV for stau_R-like and <~30 GeV for stau_L-like NLSP, m_LSP <~550 GeV in the g-2-constrained scan (2308.05723 Sec.5); ~20 GeV in SUGRA benchmarks (1704.04669 Sec.3)
Delta m > m_tau: prompt decays; Delta m < m_tau: long-lived stau covered by charged-LLP searches (2601.06358 Sec.3.4.2; 2308.05723 Fig.6)
Direct stau pair cross sections are electroweak and small; pure stau_R has no 5 sigma HL-LHC discovery reach even for large Delta m (YR as quoted in 2308.05723 Sec.5.5.1; 2403.18991 Sec.5.4)
model_dependent_predictions: Delta m up to ~60 GeV being relic-relevant requires bino-higgsino/wino mixing, which LZ direct detection largely removes for m_chi <~300 GeV (2308.05723 Sec.5)
Discovery in coannihilation models via chargino/neutralino cascades rather than direct staus (1704.04669 Sec.4: 1510-2650 fb-1 for 1tau-A)
Upper mass end of the strip (~550 GeV) depends on imposing the (now obsolete) g-2 anomaly

constraints_checked.verdict: WP25 SM prediction: Delta a_mu = 38(63)e-11, 'no tension' - g-2 motivation for light sleptons/staus is removed; 2308.05723 used WP20 value
Relic-motivated corridor is Delta m <~10 (stau_R) to <~30 GeV (stau_L); upper half of the 5-60 GeV target is not coannihilation-motivated for bino LSP
Pure-bino coannihilation points survive LZ, many below neutrino floor; mixed-LSP larger-Delta m points excluded for m_chi<~300 GeV
stau_R > 65 GeV for Delta m >~2 GeV; LHC has no sensitivity beyond LEP for 2 <~ Delta m <~ 60 GeV (Sec.3.4.4)

ISR channel alone excludes m(stau) <115 GeV at Delta m=30 GeV (degenerate L+R); combination: no exclusion (excesses, 2.7 sigma local at m=90, m_chi=40); expected combined reach just above 120 GeV - region open
77 fb-1; interpreted for chargino/neutralino with intermediate stau, not direct stau

theory_uncertainties: Signal cross section (NLO+NLL Resummino) theory error small (UNVERIFIED number) but chirality/mixing assumption changes sigma by an O(2-3) factor (UNVERIFIED); tau polarisation depends on stau mixing and chi0 composition and affects soft tau_h pT acceptance; ISR modelling of hard-jet recoil; relic-density prediction itself depends on Delta m exponentially, so the 'target' Delta m window scales with m_chi and composition.
distinctiveness: Low-moderate: soft tau_h + ISR jet + MET (or VBF) resembles W(tau nu)+jets, Z(nu nu)+jets with fake taus; no resonance or edge. Distinguishing power comes only from kinematic shape (soft tau pT, mT) at high MET.
caveats: Did not verify HL-LHC YR numbers directly (quoted via 2308.05723 and 2403.18991). Phenomenology of the corridor exists (1606.08878, 1704.04669, 2308.05723); the gap is a collaboration-level Phase-2 projection/analysis. Physically reachable target at HL-LHC is likely m(stau) ~ 100-200 GeV with Delta m ~ 5-30 GeV (UNVERIFIED; reasoned from current expected limits and cross sections), well below the ~550 GeV coannihilation upper end.
